title: Epilogue — The Drama's Done
paragraphs: "AND I ONLY AM ESCAPED ALONE TO TELL THEE" — Job.
The drama's done. Why then does anyone step forth here? Because one did survive the wreck.

It happened that after the Parsee disappeared, I was the one the Fates appointed to take the place of Ahab's bowsman, when that bowsman took over the vacant post; and I was the same man who, on the last day, when the three men were thrown out of the rocking boat, was dropped astern. So, floating on the edge of the scene that followed, and in full view of it, I was drawn, though slowly, toward the closing vortex when the half-spent suction of the sunken ship reached me. By the time I reached it, it had settled into a creamy pool. Then round and round I went, like another Ixion, always drawing closer to the button-like black bubble at the center of that slowly wheeling circle. At last, when I reached that vital center, the black bubble burst upward; and now, set free by its ingenious spring and rising with great force because of its great buoyancy, the coffin life-buoy shot lengthwise out of the sea, fell over, and floated beside me. Kept afloat by that coffin for almost a whole day and night, I drifted on a soft, dirge-like sea. The sharks glided by without harming me, as if they had padlocks on their mouths; the savage sea-hawks sailed with their beaks sheathed. On the second day a sail drew near, nearer, and picked me up at last. It was the Rachel, cruising her winding course, who in retracing her search after her missing children found only another orphan.
